To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
reading involves writing regions to a greater degree when characters were learned by writing, and this is true in Chinese as in English.
writing regions are activated during reading, and that the activation is greater for characters learned by character writing.
reading involves writing regions to a greater degree than reading, and this writing-on-reading connection is modulated both by the writing experience and the writing system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neural correlates of the reading-writing connection and the role of learning in modulating the neural signatures of the reading-writing link.
a fundamental question in cognitive science: how does the learning experience modulate neural representation?
how reading is learned and how the learning experience is represented in the brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the greater involvement of the left middle frontal region in reading Chinese characters than reading English is due to the fact that Chinese characters are learned through repeated writing, and that the reading-writing connection is language-specific.

writing regions are more activated in reading Chinese characters learned through character-writing than reading Chinese characters learned in other ways, but that this writing-related effect in reading is not specific to Chinese.

the left MGF is more involved in reading Chinese characters than English words, and that this is due to the greater involvement of writing in the reading of Chinese characters than in English reading.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
writing regions are involved in reading Chinese characters, and the degree of this involvement is modulated by how the Chinese characters were learned.
the reading-writing connection is a general feature of the reading system, which can be modulated by the experience of learning to read.
reading and writing are two interrelated processes in the human brain, and the reading-writing connection is shaped by language experience.
The main takeaway from our work is that
writing and reading share neural resources and that the learning experience shapes the neural representation of reading.
reading and writing are closely connected, and that the reading-writing connection is shaped by learning experience.
reading is not a passive process of visual perception but involves the motor system as well.
